clarify_rate_on_book_rows.explanation: Perfect clarify and sos scores are easy for a system that asks a question whenever it is unsure.

wer_normalization.code_computation_description: Case folding to lowercase, retaining alphanumeric characters and apostrophes using regex pattern [a-zA-Z0-9']+, keeping contraction tokens intact (e.g. i'm), retaining digits, stripping other punctuation, and computing macro-averaged Levenshtein edit distance over 27 non-noise evaluation clips.
wer_normalization.simple_normalization_description: Convert to lowercase, strip all punctuation including apostrophes ([^\w\s]), collapse whitespace, split into whitespace-delimited tokens, and compute word error rate.

what_the_results_mean: Language understanding on typed text works reasonably well across both methods, correctly booking 13 of 19 requests with the language model and 10 of 19 with deterministic rules.

Speech recognition on recorded audio is the primary bottleneck in the pipeline, dropping exact booking accuracy to 2 of 19 with prompt hints and 1 of 19 without hints while exhibiting word error rates of 44.4% to 55.0%.

Performance is heavily dependent on gazetteer coverage, succeeding on 11 of 12 in-vocabulary requests for the model but only 2 of 7 out-of-vocabulary requests where spoken place names lacked exact aliases.
Comparing the two text-based extractors directly on typed text, the language model (13 of 19 exact matches) outperforms the deterministic rule-based path (10 of 19 exact matches).

The rule-based path frequently asks clarifying questions when colloquial phrasing deviates from scripted regular expressions, leading to 7 clarification turns on booking requests compared to 4 for the model.
All evaluation audio clips were collected from a small sample of 30 recordings provided by only two male speakers from the same household.
Because of the small sample size and narrow acoustic distribution, these results do not claim generalization to broader commuter demographics or transit settings across Nigeria.
